milestones.title: Nuclear fission to grid power

research.what: Hahn and Strassmann observe fission in Berlin; Meitner and Frisch explain it.

change.what: Calder Hall connects to the UK grid.

milestones.note: War diverted the science into weapons first; civil power came through state programmes.

refs.label: https://www.euronuclear.org/glossary/calder-hall/

adoption.what: Nuclear supplies a significant share of electricity in leading economies.

gb.note: Nuclear provides firm low-carbon baseload on the GB grid. Ageing AGR closures and new capacity (Hinkley Point C, Sizewell C, SMRs) shape GB adequacy and inertia.

security.note: Digital instrumentation and control adds safety-critical cyber exposure.

milestones.title: HVDC transmission

research.what: Uno Lamm begins work on high-voltage mercury-arc valves at ASEA.

change.what: Gotland link enters commercial service in Sweden.

milestones.note: A long engineering road from valve research to a dependable link.

gb.note: HVDC carries GB's interconnectors and offshore wind links (e.g. Western Link, Eastern Green Link). It is central to moving Scottish and offshore wind south and easing constraints.

security.note: Adds digital control and communications to transmission and distribution assets.

milestones.title: Silicon solar cell

research.what: Bell Labs demonstrates the first practical silicon photovoltaic cell.

change.what: Vanguard 1 satellite flies on solar power.

milestones.note: Fast to first use because space could pay any price. Cheap terrestrial solar took another 50 years.

adoption.what: Solar becomes a mainstream source of new power capacity worldwide.

gb.note: GB has more than 18 GW of solar, mostly embedded on distribution networks. This drives the need for better visibility and forecasting.

security.note: Inverters and turbine controllers are networked and often vendor-managed remotely.

milestones.title: Utility-scale wind

research.what: NASA and the US energy research agency run the MOD-0 turbine programme.

change.what: First commercial wind farm opens in New Hampshire.

milestones.note: Oil shocks gave government research a sharp push into energy.

adoption.what: Wind becomes a mainstream share of new power capacity in Europe and the US.

gb.note: Wind is GB's largest renewable source, and offshore wind is central to Clean Power 2030. It drives constraint, balancing and network reinforcement needs.

security.note: Inverters and turbine controllers are networked and often vendor-managed remotely.

milestones.title: Lithium-ion battery

research.what: Goodenough’s Oxford group identifies the lithium cobalt oxide cathode.

change.what: Sony launches the first commercial lithium-ion cell.

milestones.note: The same chemistry family later made grid-scale storage viable.

milestones.title: High-temperature superconducting cable

research.what: Bednorz and Müller at IBM Zurich discover high-temperature superconductors.

change.what: A superconducting transmission cable is energised in a US utility grid.

gb.note: Could add capacity in congested urban GB networks without new rights of way. I did not confirm any GB transmission deployment.

security.note: Adds digital control and communications to transmission and distribution assets.

milestones.title: AI in grid control rooms

research.what: Machine-learning forecasting for wind, solar and demand.

change.what: AI-assisted forecasting and dispatch become routine control room tools, as NESO’s Volta programme (with Alphabet’s Tapestry on the Grand Optimiser) intends.

milestones.note: Assurance, explainability and cyber resilience will set the pace, not model capability.

basis.label: NESO: Volta programme

The Grand Optimiser sources describe design-stage deliverables (architecture plan, roadmap, interface mock-up), and NESO's innovation annex expects about 10 more Volta projects over five years. I found no source saying AI dispatch will be routine in 2027, so that year looks optimistic and the 2028–2030 range looks more likely. The 2017 researc

gb.note: NESO is building AI decision support on the Open Balancing Platform to cut balancing and constraint costs as renewable variability grows.
